html:
The war in Afghanistan began on 7 October 2001, when the United States and its allies attacked the Taliban government for sheltering al-Qaeda after the 11 September attacks. It ended with the last US troops leaving Kabul in August 2021.

The Taliban fell within weeks. Hamid Karzai led a new government, and NATO troops spread across the country. Schools reopened to girls, and Kabul grew. But the Taliban regrouped in the south and over the border in Pakistan, and the war dragged on. At its height in 2011 about 140,000 foreign troops were there.

More than 3,500 foreign soldiers and many tens of thousands of Afghans died. In 2020 the US agreed at Doha to leave. The Afghan army collapsed, and on 15 August 2021 the Taliban took Kabul again, ending in the chaos of the Kabul airlift and leading to the ban on girls' schooling.
sum: The war in Afghanistan began on 7 October 2001, when the United States and its allies attacked the Taliban government for sheltering al-Qaeda after the 11 September attacks. It ended with the last US troops leaving Kabul in August 2021.
